newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO confiscates weapons from Bosnian Serb police.
newsitem.headline: NATO confiscates weapons from Bosnian Serb police.

text.p: U.S. peacekeeping soldiers have confiscated a large cache of weapons, ammunition and explosives from Bosnian Serb special police loyal to indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic, NATO and the United Nations said on Tuesday.
The police are headed by Interior Minister Dragan Kijac who is at the heart of a struggle between President Biljana Plavsic and government hardliners trying remove her from power.

International police monitors found the unauthorised weapons on Monday during an inspection of a special police station in the northern town of Brcko in Serb-controlled territory, U.N. spokesman Alex Ivanko told Reuters.

The Serb police initially refused to hand over the weapons to international police but later backed down when American troops from the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) were called in, SFOR said in a statement.
U.S. soldiers confiscated weapons which included 82 high explosive grenades, 22 rifle grenades and an M-84 machine gun.
Police in Bosnia are forbidden to store such weapons and ammunition under terms of the 1995 Dayton peace agreement, which ended four years of war in former Yugoslavia.
"The local police told us they didn't know how the weapons ended up in the station," Ivanko said.
Kijac is loyal to former Bosnian Serb President Radovan Karadzic who was driven from public office last year as an indicted war criminal but retains backstage influence.
Plavsic precipitated a power struggle with Karadzic and his allies more than a week ago when she tried to suspend Kijac.

The special police answer exclusively to Kijac and international police officials have demanded the Bosnian Serbs agree to restructure their force so that the special police are part of a regular chain of command in the interior ministry, Ivanko said.
Kijac has repeatedly refused to reduce the size of the large police force and to introduce reforms outlined by the United Nations.

SFOR troops also confiscated weapons and ammunition at temporary checkpoints set up near Brcko on Monday. During searches of cars, U.S. soldiers found three pistols without permits and confiscated them.
No violence has erupted so far in the confrontation between the Bosnian Serb president, who enjoys support from some police units and army soldiers, and Karadzic's circle.
NATO has deployed additional troops and set up checkpoints on along main roads in Serb territory to prevent possible clashes.
The International Police Task Force said it was refusing to hold talks with Kijac and was now dealing with other officials in the interior ministry.

Plavsic, who has accused Kijac and other Karadzic loyalists of rampant corruption, dissolved parliament last week and called for new elections on September 1. The hardliners have refused to recognise her decision.
